name: Singapore — 2027-01-01 (corrected Part 4 overtime)
change_summary: Corrects the non-workman overtime hourly ceiling to SGD13.60 (monthly salary SGD2,600) and excludes managerial/executive and non-EA positions from Part 4 overtime, rest-day premiums and overtime limits. The senior-worker CPF step on 1 January 2027 (CPF Act 1953 First Schedule): above 55–60 to a 35.5% total (employer 16.5%, employee 19%, ceiling amounts 1,320/1,520, graduated coefficient 0.57) and above 60–65 to 26% (13%/13%, 1,040/1,040, 0.39); the security-sector PWM floors take their 2027 step and their 2028 step is dated inside the row, as are the 1 July 2027 and 2028 cleaning and landscape steps (MOM PWM sector pages; EPHA s.80H(2) Order). The food-services, waste-management, lift-and-escalator, administrator, driver and retail PWM floors stay at their 2026 steps and take their 1 July 2027 (retail 1 September 2027) and 1 July 2028 steps as dated steps inside pwm_wages (MOM sector pages, read 2026-10-07).

BASIC.name: Basic salary

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.20A: salary for an incomplete month is the monthly gross rate × the working days served ÷ the working days in the month (its planned WORK days; calendar days when no schedule is planned). EA s.20A(1)–(2): an incomplete month pays the monthly gross rate × days actually worked ÷ days required to work; a day required to work 5 hours or less counts as half in the days worked. EA s.20A (MOM, Monthly and daily salary: definitions and calculation, https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary, updated 8 Dec 2025, read 2026-10-08: incomplete month = monthly gross ÷ the month’s working days, public holidays included, × days worked). A complete month pays the monthly amount ÷ period.parts in each part (a semi-monthly half pays exactly half). An incomplete month (start after the 1st, exit before the last day, or a part not wholly employed) pays the monthly amount × days worked ÷ (period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days); the last part of a month the employment started before settles the month: the s.20A total (the earlier parts’ working days, this part’s worked) less what the month’s earlier slips paid for the code (earned.month), so a leaver recorded after the first half was paid is exact. A ≤ 5-hour required day counts as half in an incomplete month. No-pay and unauthorised days deduct through their own lines at the same divisor. With nothing planned, paid days ÷ the month’s calendar days.

BASIC.quantity:
!(period.covered_working_days < period.working_days
||employment.start_date > period.month_from
|| (employment.exit_date != "" && employment.exit_date < period.month_to))
  ?1.0 / double(period.parts)
  :double(period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days)
  >0.0
    ? ((double(period.parts) > 1.0 && period.part == period.parts
    &&employment.start_date <= period.month_from)
      ? (double(
        period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days
      )
      -double(period.working_days)
      + (double(period.covered_working_days)
      -0.5
      *double(
        size(
          work.days.filter(
            d,
            d.day_type == "WORK" && d.scheduled_hours > 0.0
            &&d.scheduled_hours <= 5.0
            &&d.date >= period.from
            &&d.date <= period.to
          )
        )
      )))
      /double(
        period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days
      )
      - (has(earned.month.BASIC) ? earned.month.BASIC : 0.0)
      /terms.base_salary
      : (double(period.covered_working_days)
      -0.5
      *double(
        size(
          work.days.filter(
            d,
            d.day_type == "WORK" && d.scheduled_hours > 0.0
            &&d.scheduled_hours <= 5.0
            &&d.date >= period.from
            &&d.date <= period.to
          )
        )
      ))
      /double(
        period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days
      ))
    :double(period.paid_days) / double(period.month_days)

OVERTIME.name: Overtime (1.5×)

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.38(4): overtime at not less than 1.5 times the hourly basic rate; s.38(5) and the Fourth Schedule hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44). For an eligible non-workman, the hourly basic rate for overtime is capped at SGD13.60, corresponding to the SGD2,600 monthly ceiling (MOM, Hours of work and overtime). Part 4 (EA s.35, s.2): statutory overtime applies to a workman earning ≤ $4,500 and any other employee earning ≤ $2,600 basic; outside Part 4 overtime is contractual and not priced here. A rest day (s.37(2)(c)/(3)(c)) or public holiday planned with no ordinary hours counts as overtime only its paid hours beyond the normal daily hours (employee.facts.normal_daily_hours, else the planned working shift), less any banked; the day itself is paid by REST_DAY_WORK or HOLIDAY_WORK. MOM current hours-of-work guidance: non-workman hourly basic rate is capped at SGD13.60; SGD2,600 and two overtime hours pays SGD40.80. Managers/executives and persons outside the Employment Act are not Part 4 employees. https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days ; https://www.mom.gov.sg/~/media/mom/documents/speeches/2018/guide-to-employment-act-changes-1-april-2019.pdf (retrieved 2026-10-20).

OVERTIME.quantity:
sum(
  work.days.map(
    d,
    max(
      0.0,
      ((d.scheduled_hours > 0.0
      || (d.day_type != "REST"
      &&!(d.holiday_kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"])))
        ?d.overtime_hours
        :max(
          0.0,
          d.worked_hours
          - (has(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
            ?double(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
            :size(
              work.days.filter(
                w,
                w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
              )
            )
            >0
              ?double(
                first(
                  work.days.filter(
                    w,
                    w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
                  ).map(
                    w,
                    w.scheduled_hours
                  )
                )
              )
              :0.0)
          -d.banked_hours
        ))
      -d.payable_incentive_hours
    )
  )
)

OVERTIME.name: Part-time hours beyond full-time normal hours

references.title: MOM, Overtime for part-time employees, read 2026-10-07, on the Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations: hours beyond the contracted daily hours but within a comparable full-time employee’s normal hours are paid at the hourly basic rate; hours beyond the full-time normal hours at 1.5 × it (MOM example: 4 contracted hours, 8 full-time, 9 worked = 4 × rate + 1 × 1.5 × rate). Hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × contracted weekly hours). Read on each scheduled working day from approved overtime; customer input: employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours, full_time_daily_hours (default 8, EA s.38(1)(b)).

OVERTIME.quantity:
sum(
  work.days.filter(
    d,
    d.day_type == "WORK" && d.scheduled_hours > 0.0
    &&d.overtime_hours > 0.0
  ).map(
    d,
    max(
      0.0,
      d.overtime_hours
      -max(
        0.0,
        (has(employee.facts.full_time_daily_hours)
          ?double(employee.facts.full_time_daily_hours)
          :8.0)
        -d.scheduled_hours
      )
    )
  )
)

OVERTIME.name: Part-time extra hours within full-time normal hours

references.title: MOM, Overtime for part-time employees, read 2026-10-07, on the Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations: hours beyond the contracted daily hours but within a comparable full-time employee’s normal hours are paid at the hourly basic rate; hours beyond the full-time normal hours at 1.5 × it (MOM example: 4 contracted hours, 8 full-time, 9 worked = 4 × rate + 1 × 1.5 × rate). Hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × contracted weekly hours). Read on each scheduled working day from approved overtime; customer input: employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours, full_time_daily_hours (default 8, EA s.38(1)(b)).

OVERTIME.quantity:
sum(
  work.days.filter(
    d,
    d.day_type == "WORK" && d.scheduled_hours > 0.0
    &&d.overtime_hours > 0.0
  ).map(
    d,
    min(
      d.overtime_hours,
      max(
        0.0,
        (has(employee.facts.full_time_daily_hours)
          ?double(employee.facts.full_time_daily_hours)
          :8.0)
        -d.scheduled_hours
      )
    )
  )
)

REST_DAY_WORK.name: Rest-day work (EA s.37)

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.37(2)–(3) (AGC, read 2026-10-07): a Part 4 employee who works on a rest day at his or her own request is paid half a day’s basic rate for up to half the normal hours, one day’s for more; at the employer’s request one day’s for up to half the normal hours, two days’ for more. Hours beyond the normal hours are overtime (s.37(2)(c)/(3)(c)) and priced by OVERTIME: the rest day’s paid hours beyond the normal hours. Daily basic rate per MOM: 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × days worked a week). Customer input: employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester (EMPLOYER | EMPLOYEE), required by s.37: without it the slip is held (REST_DAY_WORK_REQUESTER_MISSING); normal_daily_hours, else the planned hours of the employee’s working shift, else the slip is held (REST_DAY_NORMAL_HOURS_MISSING). Daily basic rate: 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × employee.facts.working_days_per_week); where the days a week are not recorded, the monthly basic ÷ the month’s EA s.20A working days (period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days, public holidays included; else the month’s calendar days), so the statutory day is never left unpaid.

REST_DAY_WORK.eligibility:
terms.work_classification == "EA_COVERED"
&& (employment.classification != "NON_EA"
&& ((terms.statutory_work_category != "NON_MANUAL"
&&terms.base_salary <= 4500.0)
|| (terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL"
&&terms.base_salary <= 2600.0))
&&has(employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester)
&& (has(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
  ?double(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
  :size(
    work.days.filter(w, w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0)
  )
  >0
    ?double(
      first(
        work.days.filter(
          w,
          w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
        ).map(
          w,
          w.scheduled_hours
        )
      )
    )
    :0.0)
>0.0
&&size(
  work.days.filter(d, d.day_type == "REST" && d.worked_hours > 0.0)
)
>0)
REST_DAY_WORK.quantity:
sum(
  work.days.filter(d, d.day_type == "REST" && d.worked_hours > 0.0).map(
    d,
    employee.facts.rest_day_work_requester == "EMPLOYEE"
      ? (d.worked_hours
      <= (has(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
        ?double(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
        :size(
          work.days.filter(
            w,
            w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
          )
        )
        >0
          ?double(
            first(
              work.days.filter(
                w,
                w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
              ).map(
                w,
                w.scheduled_hours
              )
            )
          )
          :0.0)
      /2.0
        ?0.5
        :1.0)
      : (d.worked_hours
      <= (has(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
        ?double(employee.facts.normal_daily_hours)
        :size(
          work.days.filter(
            w,
            w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
          )
        )
        >0
          ?double(
            first(
              work.days.filter(
                w,
                w.day_type == "WORK" && w.scheduled_hours > 0.0
              ).map(
                w,
                w.scheduled_hours
              )
            )
          )
          :0.0)
      /2.0
        ?1.0
        :2.0
  ) )
)

HOLIDAY_WORK.name: Public holiday work (extra day’s basic pay)

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.88(4)–(4A): an employee who works on a public holiday at the employer’s request is paid, besides the gross rate for the day, an extra day’s salary at the basic rate of pay (MOM, Public holidays: entitlement and pay, https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/public-holidays-entitlement-and-pay). MOM, Monthly and daily salary (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary): the daily basic rate is 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × the average days the employee is required to work a week). A roster day on a published public or substitute holiday is the work; time off in lieu by agreement is not priced. Part-time employees are paid under the Part-Time Regulations and are not priced here. s.88(4A): an employee outside Part 4 (not a s.35 workman or s.35(b) employee) may instead be given a day off, or part of one, in lieu of the extra day’s salary; record such time off and void the line rather than paying both. Daily basic rate: 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × employee.facts.working_days_per_week); where the days a week are not recorded, the monthly basic ÷ the month’s EA s.20A working days (period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days, public holidays included; else the month’s calendar days), so the statutory day is never left unpaid.

HOLIDAY_WORK.eligibility:
employment.classification != "NON_EA"
&&terms.employment_type != "PART_TIME"
&&size(
  work.holidays.filter(
    h,
    h.worked && h.kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"]
    && (h.given_to != "ONLY_IF_OFF_ON_REPLACED_DATE"
    || (h.replaces != "" && !(h.replaces in work.dates
  ) )))
)
>0

HOLIDAY_WORK.name: Part-time public holiday work

references.title: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations; MOM, Public holidays for part-time employees (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/part-time-employment/public-holidays, read 2026-10-07): a part-timer required to work on a public holiday is paid, besides the holiday entitlement, the basic rate of pay for one day’s work — the day’s hours at the hourly basic rate 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × contracted weekly hours). Customer input: employee.facts.part_time_weekly_hours.

HOLIDAY_WORK.quantity:
sum(
  work.days.filter(
    d,
    has(d.holiday_kind)
    &&d.holiday_kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"]
    &&d.worked_hours > 0.0
  ).map(
    d,
    d.scheduled_hours > 0.0 ? d.scheduled_hours : d.worked_hours
  )
)

PAID_HOLIDAY.name: Public holiday on a non-working day

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.88(1)(c) (AGC, read 2026-10-07): if a public holiday falls on a day the employee is not required to work, the employer either pays the holiday at the gross rate of pay or gives a day off in substitution. Priced at the gross daily rate unless employee.facts.ph_off_day_compensation is DAY_OFF (customer input: then credit PUBLIC_HOLIDAY_IN_LIEU). A holiday on the rest day moves to the next working day (s.88(1)(b)); the gazetted Sunday substitutes are in the public_holidays calendar. https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968 EA s.20A divisor (MOM, Monthly and daily salary: definitions and calculation (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary, updated 8 Dec 2025, read 2026-10-08): incomplete month = monthly gross ÷ the month’s working days × days worked, the working days excluding rest and non-working days but including public holidays): period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days, the whole calendar month’s, the same in every part; with nothing planned, the month’s calendar days.

PAID_HOLIDAY.quantity:
double(
  size(
    work.days.filter(
      d,
      has(d.holiday_kind)
      &&d.holiday_kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"]
      &&d.day_type == "OFF"
      &&!d.worked
    )
  )
)

PAID_HOLIDAY.name: Holiday pay forfeited for an adjacent unauthorised absence

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.88(3): an employee absent without the employer's prior consent or reasonable excuse on the working day immediately before or after a public holiday is not entitled to holiday pay for it. Customer input: the roster day's facts.unauthorised_absence. Deducted at the gross daily rate per holiday. https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968 EA s.20A divisor (MOM, Monthly and daily salary: definitions and calculation (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary, updated 8 Dec 2025, read 2026-10-08): incomplete month = monthly gross ÷ the month’s working days × days worked, the working days excluding rest and non-working days but including public holidays): period.month_working_days + period.month_holiday_work_days, the whole calendar month’s, the same in every part; with nothing planned, the month’s calendar days.

PAID_HOLIDAY.quantity:
double(
  size(
    work.days.filter(
      h,
      has(h.holiday_kind)
      &&h.holiday_kind in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE"]
      &&!h.worked
      &&work.days.exists(
        a,
        a.day_type == "WORK" && !has(a.holiday_kind)
        &&has(a.facts.unauthorised_absence)
        &&a.facts.unauthorised_absence == true
        && ((a.date < h.date
        &&!work.days.exists(
          b,
          b.day_type == "WORK" && !has(b.holiday_kind)
          &&b.date > a.date
          &&b.date < h.date
        ))
        || (a.date > h.date
        &&!work.days.exists(
          b,
          b.day_type == "WORK" && !has(b.holiday_kind)
          &&b.date < a.date
          &&b.date > h.date
        )
      ) ))
    )
  )
)

entries.instructions: Ministry of Manpower, Employment Act 1968 pay and leave items. Under Employment practices > Leave: annual, sick and hospitalisation leave (service bands, eligibility and approval conditions such as medical certification) and Employment Act maternity and childcare leave for a non-citizen child. Under Employment practices > Salary and Hours of work, rest day and public holidays: the pay for overtime, rest-day work and public-holiday work and the gross / basic rate definitions the work items are built from, plus AWS and bonus pages. Under Termination: retrenchment benefit, salary in lieu of notice and other termination payments; the Retirement and Re-employment Act Employment Assistance Payment (Tripartite Guidelines PDF linked from Employment practices > Re-employment); suspension pending a misconduct inquiry (Termination of employment pages; site search "misconduct"); kinds of permitted deductions (loans, advances, recoveries) in the Salary topic's deductions page; pro-rated leave and pay for part-timers under the Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations page.

Government-Paid Leave portal (Ministry of Social and Family Development), Child Development Co-Savings Act schemes for a citizen child. Open Schemes for each scheme page: Government-Paid Maternity, Paternity, Shared Parental, Adoption and Childcare Leave, Extended Childcare Leave and Unpaid Infant Care Leave — eligibility, weeks or days by the child's birth date, splitting between parents and which leave the employer pays and the government reimburses (reimbursement caps).

Central Provident Fund Board employer pages for CPF contributions: rate tables by age band and citizen / SPR year (the yearly contribution-rate PDF under Employer obligations > How much CPF contributions to pay), the Ordinary and Additional Wage ceilings, wage bands and rounding, and which payments attract CPF (including NS make-up pay and termination payments). Also the Skills Development Levy (rate, minimum and maximum) and the self-help-group fund schedules and opt-out rules (CDAC, ECF, MBMF, SINDA) under Employer obligations > Contributions to self-help groups. Check the effective date on each table; senior-worker rate steps appear in the service FAQ articles before the PDF is published.

Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, employment income tax as it touches payroll. Under Taxes > Individual income tax > Employers: taxable versus exempt allowances and benefits (the tax base). Under Taxes > Withholding tax: withholding on payments to non-resident directors and public entertainers (Section 45) — rates and base. Resident employees have no monthly withholding.
Ministry of Manpower, Passes and permits: the foreign worker levy for Work Permit and S Pass holders — tiers, quota-linked rates and how the levy is charged per month.

Ministry of Manpower, limits under the Employment Act 1968 and related law. Contract coverage: Part 4 salary thresholds, workman / non-workman, managers and executives (Employment Act coverage pages). Employment practices > Salary: salary period and payment deadlines, deduction ceilings. Hours of work, rest day and overtime: daily and weekly hours, the monthly overtime cap, rest-day frequency. The Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations hour threshold, young persons and children limits, Retirement and Re-employment Act minimum retirement and re-employment ages, the Progressive Wage Model sector and occupational wage floors and the Local Qualifying Salary (Employment practices > Progressive Wage Model), and how long employment records must be kept.
Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore: how long employers must keep payroll and tax records (site search "record keeping" from Taxes > Individual income tax > Employers).

Personal Data Protection Commission: the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 retention limitation obligation as it applies to employee data. Use Overview of PDPA > The legislation and the advisory guidelines chapter on employment under Guidelines and consultation.

Ministry of Manpower, event rules under the Employment Act 1968. Employment practices > Public holidays: what follows when a public holiday falls on a rest day or non-working day, or the employee works it. Leave pages: what happens to leave and pay when an exit occurs mid-year (encashment or offset of unused annual leave). Termination: notice and salary in lieu, payment of salary on dismissal, resignation, retrenchment or death and its deadlines.

Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, Taxes > Individual income tax > Employers > Tax clearance for foreign & SPR employees (IR21): what an exit of a non-citizen employee must cause on payroll — withholding all monies due from the notice date until clearance.
Government-Paid Leave portal: under Schemes, what an employer must still pay or keep when employment ends, the employee is dismissed or a leave block spans an exit or a new child's birth date.

Ministry of Manpower, employer duties with deadlines: key employment terms in writing, itemised payslips and employment records (Employment practices > Salary > Itemised payslips and Employment records), mandatory retrenchment notification, flexible work arrangement request handling and fair employment / Workplace Fairness legislation duties, work pass security bond and medical insurance (Passes and permits), and work injury compensation insurance and workplace incident reporting (Workplace safety and health). Newsroom > Press releases dates a change; the topic page states the operative duty.

Central Provident Fund Board employer obligations: CPF, SDL and self-help-group payment due date, the submission (e-Submit / CPF EZPay) process, late-payment interest and penalties, and new-employer registration for a CPF Submission Number.

Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, Taxes > Individual income tax > Employers: the Auto-Inclusion Scheme and Form IR8A filing deadline, Appendix 8A (benefits in kind) and 8B (share gains), Form IR21 filing deadlines for departing non-citizen employees, and Taxes > Withholding tax: Section 45 filing and payment deadlines.

Personal Data Protection Commission, Personal Data Protection Act 2012 duties over employee data: purpose notification and the employment exceptions to consent, appointing a data protection officer, access and correction request time limits, and data breach assessment and notification to PDPC and affected employees. Use Overview of PDPA > The legislation and the employment chapter of the advisory guidelines under Guidelines and consultation.
Government-Paid Leave portal: under Schemes and the employer claim pages, how and by when an employer claims government reimbursement and the records it must keep.

Ministry of Manpower, Employment practices > Salary: the monthly-wage basis (the incomplete-month formula and the hourly and daily basic rate formulas), the salary period and pay date the version's settings use, and how a shortfall or final settlement may be carried (negative net, exit handling). Passes and permits: the work pass types an employee record must hold.

Central Provident Fund Board employer pages: the employer and employee facts CPF and self-help-group computation needs — CPF Submission Number, citizenship or SPR status and year, date of birth for age bands, and the race / religion that selects the fund.

Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore: the currency and the Year of Assessment basis for employment income (calendar-year income), the employer tax reference number, the employee identification numbers IR8A requires and the tax-residency test (Taxes > Individual income tax; Employers > Filing employee earnings for the IR8A fields).

uen.title: Unique Entity Number
uen.description: ACRA UEN: the employer’s IRAS tax reference for AIS (Form IR8A) and IR21 filing, and its MOM employer identity for work passes and the foreign worker levy.

cpf_submission_number.title: CPF Submission Number (CSN)
cpf_submission_number.description: CPF Board CSN: the UEN (9–10 characters), payment type and serial number, written UEN-TYPE-SERIAL (e.g. 201912345A-PTE-01): the account the month’s CPF, SDL and self-help-group contributions are submitted under, and every record of the CPF EZPay (FTP) file (EXPORTS CPF_EZPAY_FTP).

foreign_worker_levy_payer.title: Pays the foreign worker levy
foreign_worker_levy_payer.description: True while the entity employs any S Pass or Work Permit holder; false stops the monthly FOREIGN_WORKER_LEVY obligation. Unrecorded raises it.

ns_direct_scheme.description: Registered for MINDEF/MHA DIRECT (Direct Reimbursement to Employers of Claims for NS Training): the employer keeps paying wages during NS training and is reimbursed (NS_LEAVE pay_fraction 1); otherwise NS days are an incomplete month under EA s.20A(1)(d) (pay_fraction 0). Customer input.

industrial_undertaking.description: The entity is an industrial undertaking (EA s.2) for the young-person notification. Customer input.

dpo_contact.description: Business contact of the designated data protection officer (PDPA s.11(5)). Customer input.

full_time_weekly_hours.description: The entity’s normal full-time week in hours: the comparable full-time hours a part-timer’s leave is prorated against when the employee records none (Part-Time Regulations reg.7). Customer input.

employment_type.description: PART_TIME is an employee contracted to work under 35 hours a week (Employment Act 1968 s.66A; Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations reg.2): the PT_ANNUAL_HOURLY_* allowances and the EAP part-time pro-ration read it; HOLIDAY_WORK does not price it.

work_classification.description: NON_EA is outside the Employment Act 1968 (s.2: seafarers, domestic workers, statutory-board and civil servants): statutory leave, holiday work and the EA deductions are not offered. MANAGERIAL is a manager or executive, covered by the Act but not by Part 4.

statutory_work_category.description: Employment Act 1968 s.2 workman (manual labour or its supervision) or not: OVERTIME computes a non-workman’s rate on at most SGD 2,600 (s.38(8), Fourth Schedule).

residency_status.description: CPF and the self-help-group funds charge only a Singapore Citizen or SPR (CPF Act 1953 s.7); a FOREIGNER pays SDL only. NS leave and EAP read it.

residency_since.description: SPR status grant date: the CPF graduated first- and second-year rates run from it (First Schedule Tables 2–3).

mom_declared_monthly_salary.description: The fixed monthly salary declared to MOM for the employee’s Employment Pass or S Pass (MOM_DECLARED_SALARY). Customer input.

pwm_role.description: The employee’s Progressive Wage Model role and job level (PWM_WAGE_FLOOR reads PAYROLL pwm_wages). Customer input.

notice_period_days.description: The written contractual notice period in days, the same for both parties (EA s.10(2)); when absent, salary in lieu of notice is at least the s.10(3) period. Customer input.

race.description: The employee’s race as CPF records it (for example CHINESE, MALAY, INDIAN, EURASIAN): the CDAC, ECF and SINDA self-help-group funds read it (CPF Act 1953 s.77(1)(p)).

religion.description: The employee’s religion (ISLAM for a Muslim employee): the Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF) reads it.

solo_parent.description: A sole parent: the shared parental leave pool defaults to the whole pool on an individual arrangement (Child Development Co-Savings Act 2001 ss.12DA–12DD).

fixed_term.description: A fixed-term contract: while true the employment is not permanent (`permanent_when`).

exit_facts.description: Stored on employment_contract.exit_facts when the contract closes (CEL employment.exit_facts).

dismissed_for_misconduct.title: Dismissed for misconduct after due inquiry
dismissed_for_misconduct.description: Employment Act 1968 s.14(1) (due inquiry) with s.88A: untaken annual leave is paid on every exit except a DISMISSAL for misconduct; the encash-leave-on-exit rule withholds it when this is true on a DISMISSAL.

notice_served.title: Resignation notice served in full
notice_served.description: Employment Act 1968 s.23: served, salary is due on the last day; not served, within 7 days.

final_pay_not_possible.title: Pay on the dismissal day not possible
final_pay_not_possible.description: Employment Act 1968 s.22: then within 3 days, excluding rest days and public holidays.

eap_decision.description: Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993 s.7C: AWARD when an eligible employee could not be re-employed and no alternate-employer offer was accepted; EMPLOYMENT_ASSISTANCE_PAYMENT is offered only then.

eap_contract_retirement_months.description: A contractual retirement age above the statutory one, in months of age.

eap_contract_reemployment_months.description: A contractual re-employment age above the statutory one, in months of age.

eap_gross_monthly.description: Last drawn monthly gross pay (Tripartite Guidelines).

eap_previous_gross_monthly.description: Gross before a transfer to a lower-paid job within 3 months of the exit.

eap_prorate_bounds.description: Pro-rate the EAP minimum and maximum for a part-time employee.

retrenchment_notified_on.title: Employees notified of the retrenchment on
retrenchment_notified_on.description: MOM mandatory retrenchment notification: due within 5 working days after this day (RETRENCHMENT_NOTIFICATION).

ir21_clearance_on.title: IRAS tax clearance received on
ir21_clearance_on.description: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(7) / EA s.24: the day the Comptroller’s clearance (or permission to pay) arrived; until it is recorded the final pay of a non-Citizen is held (IR21_FINAL_PAY_HOLD).

ir21_exemption.description: IRAS, Tax clearance for employees: no IR21 for an SPR not leaving Singapore permanently who gives a letter of undertaking, for an employment of 60 days or less (not a director), or for income below $21,000 a year under the IRAS conditions. Recorded, the IR21 task is not raised and the final pay is released. Customer input.

ir21_additional_clearance_on.title: IRAS clearance of the Additional/Amended IR21 received on
ir21_additional_clearance_on.description: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(7); IRAS, Tax clearance for employees: a payment after the IR21 clearance waits for clearance of an Additional/Amended Form IR21; until this is recorded such a payment is held (IR21_ADDITIONAL_PAYMENT_HOLD).

sdl_household_role.description: SDL Act 1979 s.2: a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual otherwise than in connection with a trade, business, profession or vocation is not an “employee” (with sdl_wholly_exclusive and sdl_nonbusiness true).

sdl_nonbusiness.description: Employed otherwise than in connection with the employer’s trade, business, profession or vocation (SDL Act s.2).

sdl_service_scope.description: SDL Act 1979 s.2 “employee”: one rendering services wholly or partly in Singapore in the month (or on leave attributable to such services). OUTSIDE_SINGAPORE: none in the month — no levy.

sdl_student_class.description: Recorded only; no SDL exemption for students was found in the SDL Act (read 2026-10-07), so no rule reads it.

sdl_wholly_exclusive.description: Wholly and exclusively employed by the individual employer (SDL Act s.2).

spr_full_rates.title: SPR full rates jointly elected (CPF)
spr_full_rates.description: CPF Board: an SPR in the first or second year of status and the employer may jointly apply to contribute at the full (Table 1) rates; record it on the CPF standing from the month the Board approves. The employer-only full / employee graduated (F/G) election is not applied.

spr_employer_full_rates.title: SPR employer full rate elected (CPF, F/G)
spr_employer_full_rates.description: CPF Board Tables 4–5: the employer of an SPR in the first or second year of status may apply to contribute at the full employer rate while the employee stays on the graduated rate; record it on the CPF standing from the month the Board approves. spr_full_rates (both full) takes precedence.

shg_opted_out.description: CPF Board, Contributions to self-help groups: an employee who opts out of a fund in writing (the fund’s form) stops its deduction from the effective date recorded as the standing’s effective_range.from. Set on that fund’s standing (CDAC, ECF, MBMF or SINDA).

shg_monthly_amount.description: A changed monthly contribution the employee instructed through the fund, in place of the schedule amount, on that fund’s standing.

facts.description: Person facts stored beside employment_statutory_facts on employment_profile.facts (CEL employee.facts.*).

working_days_per_week.title: Average days required to work a week
working_days_per_week.description: MOM, Monthly and daily salary: a monthly-rated employee’s daily basic rate is 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × the average number of days the employee is required to work a week). HOLIDAY_WORK prices only when it is recorded (CEL employee.facts.working_days_per_week).

immigration_status.title: Singapore immigration status
immigration_status.description: MOM work pass types (https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits). The hire and exit obligation rules read it (IR21 for every non-Citizen; work pass in force and cancellation for a pass holder); keep it consistent with the contract terms’ residency_status, which those rules cannot see.

rest_day_work_requester.description: EA s.37(2)–(3): who asks the employee to work on rest days, which sets the rest-day pay (REST_DAY_WORK). Customer input.

normal_daily_hours.description: The employee’s normal hours of work for one day (EA s.37: half of them is the rest-day pay threshold). Customer input.

part_time_weekly_hours.description: Contracted weekly hours of a part-time employee (under 35, EA s.66A): the hourly basic rate divisor for PART_TIME_HOLIDAY_WORK. Customer input.

tax_resident.description: Income Tax Act 1947 s.2: Singapore tax resident. A non-resident director’s fees are withheld at 24% (WHT_NR_DIRECTOR). Customer input.

leaves_singapore_from.description: Day a non-Citizen employee is posted overseas or leaves Singapore for more than 3 months while employed (IR21_LEAVING_SINGAPORE). Customer input.

ph_off_day_compensation.description: EA s.88(1)(c): a public holiday on a non-working day is paid at the gross rate (PAY) or given as a day off in substitution (DAY_OFF). Customer input.

full_time_daily_hours.description: Normal daily hours of a comparable full-time employee (default 8, EA s.38(1)(b)): a part-timer’s hours beyond them are paid at 1.5 × the hourly basic rate, those between the contracted and these hours at the plain rate (PART_TIME_EXTRA_HOURS, PART_TIME_OVERTIME). Customer input.

full_time_weekly_hours.description: Weekly hours of a similar full-time employee, against which a part-timer’s leave is prorated (Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations reg.7); else the entity’s full_time_weekly_hours, else 44 (reg.2(2), no similar full-time employee). Customer input.
